narrative_purpose: Anchor the cold open: the reader counts four wings and jumps to the wrong conclusion. The figure must make the four-surface arrangement unmistakable while the animal is doing something only an agile flyer could do.
subject: A large dark four-winged predator turning hard, seen from slightly below and behind so both wing pairs are visible at once. The front pair is at the bottom of its downstroke, angled steeply; the rear pair, mounted well behind on the body and clearly separate, is at the top of its upstroke. A forward-projecting bone horn on the skull. A small Na'vi rider pressed low along its neck.
scene: The interior of a drifting volcanic ash plume above broken basalt, coarse grit hanging in the air, dark cliff faces half-visible to one side, no horizon.
camera: Slightly below and behind the banking animal, close enough that the wing roots and the separation between the two pairs are legible.
light: Weak diffuse light through ash, plus a low ember-orange underlight that skims the wing membranes from beneath and separates the four surfaces from each other.
palette: Charcoal and ash-grey animal with deep crimson striations, cool indigo dust, a single warm ember accent from below.
style: Painterly naturalist plate, the mood tense and observed rather than heroic.
detail_level: High detail on the wing roots, membrane texture and horn; the plume and cliffs soft and hazed.
composition: Animal on a rising diagonal, one large area of plain dark hazy plume in the lower left and one along the upper right kept plain and low-detail so overlaid callouts stay readable.
consistency_notes: Same animal as the cover: two fully developed pairs of driven membranous wings caught on opposite strokes, no walking hind limbs, forward bone horn, charcoal-and-crimson colouring. The separation between front and rear wing pairs must be obvious at a glance - this is the whole point of the picture.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no diagram overlays, no green rainforest, no neon glow, no 3D-render or photographic look, no cartoon style, no single wing pair
